pinyin: shèng bài nǎi bīng jiā cháng shì
literal: win · lose · is · soldiers · common · matter
natural: victory and defeat are everyday matters for soldiers

meaning.en: Winning and losing are normal in any contest, so a setback is no reason to despair.
meaning.zh: 打仗有胜有败是常有的事，比喻一时失败不必气馁。

equivalents: you win some, you lose some
a setback is part of the game

examples.zh: 胜败乃兵家常事，输了这场还有下一场。
examples.en: Wins and losses come with the territory; after this defeat there is the next match.

examples.zh: 教练安慰队员：胜败乃兵家常事，不要灰心。
examples.en: The coach consoled the players: victory and defeat are all in the game, so don't lose heart.

usage.en: Consoling or self-consoling after failure in sport, business or exams; the tone is calm, sometimes wry.
usage.zh: 多用于比赛、生意、考试失败后的宽慰或自我安慰。

synonyms: 胜败兵家事不期，包羞忍耻是男儿

natural: respectfully take the last seat

meaning.en: To sit in the lowest seat at a banquet; a polite way of saying one is present as the humblest guest.
meaning.zh: 谦称自己在宴席上坐在末座，是客套话。

equivalents: be honoured to bring up the rear

examples.zh: 我只是敬陪末座，各位前辈请多指教。
examples.en: I'm only here to take the lowest seat; seniors, please advise me.

examples.zh: 今天的晚宴，我这个晚辈敬陪末座。
examples.en: At tonight's dinner, I, as the youngest, take the last seat.

usage.en: Polite-humble formula used by the speaker about himself, not of others. Also written 忝陪末座 or 叨陪末座.
usage.zh: 谦辞，用于自称，不用于称他人。也作“忝陪末座”“叨陪末座”。

natural: beyond one person there is another

meaning.en: However good you are, there is always someone better.
meaning.zh: 一个人不管多么出色，总有比他更强的人，劝人不要骄傲。

examples.zh: 人外有人，天外有天，别太骄傲。
examples.en: There's always someone better, so don't be so proud.

examples.zh: 参加比赛才知道人外有人。
examples.en: Taking part in the contest taught me there is always someone better.

usage.en: Usually said together with 天外有天; a humbling reminder.
usage.zh: 常与“天外有天”连用，用来劝人谦虚。

pinyin: shàng qì bù jiē xià qì
literal: upper · breath · not · connect · lower · breath
natural: the upper breath doesn't meet the lower breath

meaning.en: Out of breath; panting hard.
meaning.zh: 喘得很厉害，气都接不上。

examples.zh: 他跑上五楼，累得上气不接下气。
examples.en: He ran up to the fifth floor and was gasping for breath.

examples.zh: 笑得上气不接下气，眼泪都出来了。
examples.en: She laughed so hard she could hardly breathe.

usage.en: Describes exhaustion or laughing; often after 累得/笑得/跑得.
usage.zh: 多说“累得/笑得/跑得上气不接下气”。

natural: radiance that lights up others

meaning.en: Dazzling, radiant and striking to look at.
meaning.zh: 形容人容光焕发、非常美丽或出色。

examples.zh: 新娘穿着婚纱，光彩照人。
examples.en: The bride in her wedding dress looked radiant.

examples.zh: 她获奖后在台上光彩照人。
examples.en: On stage after winning the prize she was dazzling.

usage.en: Praise, usually of a person's appearance; can also describe an achievement.
usage.zh: 褒义，多形容人的外貌，也可形容成就。

natural: trace a river to its source and follow its flow

meaning.en: To investigate a matter thoroughly, tracing it from its origin through its development.
meaning.zh: 追根究底，从源头一直考察到流变。

equivalents: go to the bottom of things

examples.zh: 这位学者穷源溯流，写出了该词的完整演变史。
examples.en: The scholar traced the word from its source and wrote its complete history.

examples.zh: 研究汉字要穷源溯流，才能真正理解它的意义。
examples.en: To study characters you must trace them from the source to understand their meaning.

usage.en: Scholarly and literary; about research methods.
usage.zh: 书面语，多用于治学、研究。

natural: food spread ten feet square before one

meaning.en: An extravagantly rich banquet, with dishes covering a table ten feet square.
meaning.zh: 面前摆满一丈见方的美食，形容饮食极其奢侈。

equivalents: a banquet fit for a king

examples.zh: 富豪的宴会上，食前方丈，极尽奢华。
examples.en: The tycoon's banquet was a lavish spread of every luxury.

examples.zh: 他虽食前方丈，仍然觉得没胃口。
examples.en: Though a mighty feast lay before him, he had no appetite.

story.en: Mencius listed things he would not do even if he gained power: 'a table ten feet square, hundreds of concubines' (食前方丈，侍妾数百人，我得志，弗为也).
story.zh: 孟子说：“食前方丈，侍妾数百人，我得志，弗为也。”

usage.en: Literary; implies luxury and often criticism of waste.
usage.zh: 书面语，含奢侈之意，常带批评。

natural: scratch the head and pace back and forth

meaning.en: To scratch one's head and dither, anxious and unsure; originally of a lover waiting.
meaning.zh: 抓着头发来回徘徊，形容心里焦急或犹豫不决，原指等待情人。

examples.zh: 他站在门口搔首踟蹰，不知该不该进去。
examples.en: He stood at the door scratching his head, unsure whether to go in.

examples.zh: 考试前夜，她搔首踟蹰，难以入睡。
examples.en: The night before the exam she paced about restlessly and couldn't sleep.

story.en: In 'The Quiet Girl' a young man cannot find his sweetheart at the tryst: 'I love her but can't see her, I scratch my head and pace' (爱而不见，搔首踟蹰).

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Literary. In the Book of Songs it describes a young man waiting for his sweetheart.
usage.zh: 书面语。《诗经》中形容男子等待心上人。

pinyin: yǐ yī bān kuī quán bào
literal: by · one · spot · peep at · whole · leopard
natural: judge the whole leopard by one spot

meaning.en: To infer the whole from a small part.
meaning.zh: 从看到的一小部分推知事物的全貌。

equivalents: judge the whole by a part

examples.zh: 从这一页稿子，就可以以一斑窥全豹，看出作者的功力。
examples.en: From this single page you can judge the whole and see the author's skill.

examples.zh: 不能以一斑窥全豹，只凭一次见面就下结论。
examples.en: You can't judge the whole from a part; don't reach a verdict after a single meeting.

usage.en: Can be positive (insight) or a caution against hasty judgement; close to 管中窥豹.
usage.zh: 可表示见微知著，也可警示以偏概全；与“管中窥豹”相近。

natural: blame for seeking perfection

meaning.en: Criticism that comes from demanding perfection, even when one has done well.
meaning.zh: 因为过分苛求完美而招来的指责。

examples.zh: 做事难免有缺点，不能有求全之毁。
examples.en: Nobody is perfect; one shouldn't be harshly judged for falling short of perfection.

examples.zh: 他尽了力，却仍遭求全之毁。
examples.en: He did his best but was still blamed for not being perfect.

story.en: Mencius observed: 'There is praise one did not expect, and blame that comes from seeking perfection' (有不虞之誉，有求全之毁).
story.zh: 孟子说：“有不虞之誉，有求全之毁。”

usage.en: Usually paired with 不虞之誉. Literary; used to comment on unfair criticism.
usage.zh: 常与“不虞之誉”连用，书面语，用于评论不公平的指责。

natural: continue what is broken off and prop up what falls

meaning.en: To restore lines that have died out and support what is about to collapse.
meaning.zh: 接续断绝的事业，扶持将倒的局面，指救助危亡。

equivalents: restore the fallen and rescue the failing

examples.zh: 明君当继绝扶倾，保全弱小之国。
examples.en: A wise ruler should preserve fallen houses and support small states in danger.

examples.zh: 她一生致力于继绝扶倾，保护濒危的民间技艺。
examples.en: All her life she worked to save fading folk crafts from extinction.

usage.en: Literary; praises rescue of the endangered, whether states, lineages or traditions.
usage.zh: 书面语，褒义，用于救助濒危的国家、世系或传统。

natural: draped in red and hung with green

meaning.en: Decked out in bright, festive colours, whether of clothes or decorations.
meaning.zh: 穿戴或装饰得红红绿绿，十分鲜艳喜庆。

examples.zh: 过年了，大街小巷披红挂绿，十分热闹。
examples.en: For the New Year the streets were hung with red and green and full of cheer.

examples.zh: 孩子们披红挂绿，扮成戏里的角色。
examples.en: The children, rigged out in bright colours, dressed up as characters in the opera.

usage.en: Can be festive, or mildly mocking for gaudy dress.
usage.zh: 可形容节日喜庆，也可略带讽刺地指穿着艳俗。

natural: bird in a cage, ape in a pen

meaning.en: Someone deprived of freedom, like a caged bird or penned monkey.
meaning.zh: 比喻失去自由、受到拘束的人。

equivalents: a bird in a gilded cage

examples.zh: 他在公司里如笼鸟槛猿，一点自由都没有。
examples.en: At the company he was a caged bird without any freedom.

examples.zh: 她觉得自己困在家里，像笼鸟槛猿。
examples.en: Stuck at home, she felt like a bird in a cage.

usage.en: Literary and sympathetic; describes loss of freedom.
usage.zh: 书面语，带同情，形容失去自由。

natural: go for the real thing

meaning.en: To stop joking and get serious; to do it in earnest.
meaning.zh: 不再是闹着玩，认真起来真干。

examples.zh: 老板这次动真格的了，迟到要扣工资。
examples.en: The boss means business this time: lateness will cost pay.

examples.zh: 光说不练不行，该动真格的了。
examples.en: Talk isn't enough; it's time to do it for real.

usage.en: Colloquial; 真格 means 'for real'. Often in a warning or resolve.
usage.zh: 口语，“真格”指真的，常用于警告或表明决心。

natural: tenderness like water

meaning.en: Tender and gentle feelings, flowing like water.
meaning.zh: 情意温柔缠绵，像水一样。

examples.zh: 她望着孩子，眼里柔情似水。
examples.en: She looked at her child with tenderness in her eyes.

examples.zh: 他对妻子柔情似水，体贴入微。
examples.en: He is tender to his wife and attentive to every detail.

origin.source: 宋·秦观《鹊桥仙·纤云弄巧》

story.en: Qin Guan's lyric on the Weaver Girl and Cowherd: 'Tender feelings are like water, the happy meeting like a dream' (柔情似水，佳期如梦).
story.zh: 秦观《鹊桥仙》：“柔情似水，佳期如梦，忍顾鹊桥归路。”

usage.en: Mostly about women and love, but also parents and children; poetic.
usage.zh: 多形容女子或爱情，也可用于亲子之情，富诗意。

natural: cultivate yourself through stillness

meaning.en: Self-cultivation comes through quiet reflection.
meaning.zh: 通过静心思考来修养自身。

equivalents: calm the mind to improve oneself

examples.zh: 静以修身，俭以养德，这是诸葛亮留给儿子的家训。
examples.en: 'Be still to cultivate yourself, thrifty to nurture virtue': Zhuge Liang's family precept for his son.

examples.zh: 他把“静以修身”写在书房墙上。
examples.en: He wrote 'cultivate yourself through stillness' on his study wall.

story.en: Zhuge Liang advised his son: 'The gentleman's conduct is to cultivate himself through stillness and nurture virtue through thrift' (君子之行，静以修身，俭以养德).
story.zh: 诸葛亮《诫子书》：“君子之行，静以修身，俭以养德。”

usage.en: Usually quoted with 俭以养德 as a motto for personal discipline.
usage.zh: 常与“俭以养德”并称，作为自律座右铭。

natural: the good rule of Emperors Wen and Jing

meaning.en: The prosperous reigns of Emperor Wen and Emperor Jing of the Western Han (180–141 BC).
meaning.zh: 指西汉文帝、景帝时期（前180—前141年）的清明盛世，减轻赋税，休养生息。

equivalents: a golden age of light taxes and peace

examples.zh: 汉初经过文景之治，国力大增。
examples.en: After the rule of Wen and Jing the early Han grew much stronger.

examples.zh: 历史课上，老师讲到了文景之治的轻徭薄赋政策。
examples.en: In history class the teacher covered the light taxes and corvée of the Wen–Jing era.

usage.en: A historical term of praise for an era of recovery and light burdens, often compared with later prosperous ages.
usage.zh: 历史专有名词，赞扬休养生息的盛世，常与后世盛世并提。

natural: the great recluse hides in the city

meaning.en: A true recluse retreats inwardly while living in the busy world, not in the mountains.
meaning.zh: 真正的隐士不必隐居深山，在喧闹的城市里也能保持内心清静。

equivalents: the true hermit lives in the crowd
be still in the midst of bustle

examples.zh: 大隐隐于市，他在闹市里开了一间小书店。
examples.en: A true recluse hides in the city; he opened a small bookshop in the busy centre.

examples.zh: 她说自己大隐隐于市，下班后谁也不见。
examples.en: She says she is a hermit in the city and sees no one after work.

story.en: Wang Kangju wrote: 'The small recluse hides in hills and marshes; the great recluse hides in court and market' (小隐隐陵薮，大隐隐朝市).
story.zh: 王康琚《反招隐诗》：“小隐隐陵薮，大隐隐朝市。”

usage.en: The modern form 大隐隐于市 is a paraphrase of the classical 大隐隐朝市. Often said half-jokingly of quiet people in cities.
usage.zh: 今通行说法“大隐隐于市”由“大隐隐朝市”演变而来，常半开玩笑地形容在城市里低调生活的人。

natural: Heaven grants what people wish

meaning.en: Things turn out just as one hoped.
meaning.zh: 事情的发展正合人们的心愿。

examples.zh: 天遂人愿，比赛那天终于放晴了。
examples.en: As we wished, it finally cleared up on match day.

examples.zh: 祝你们天遂人愿，早日成家。
examples.en: May all your wishes come true and may you soon start a family.

usage.en: Often used in good wishes or when luck follows hope.
usage.zh: 常用于祝愿，或表示机缘巧合如愿。

natural: talk of heroes over heated wine

meaning.en: To discuss heroes and affairs of the world over wine; alludes to Cao Cao and Liu Bei.
meaning.zh: 边喝酒边评论天下英雄，典出曹操与刘备。

equivalents: chew over great men over a drink

examples.zh: 几位朋友煮酒论英雄，从历史聊到当下。
examples.en: Some friends chatted about heroes over wine, from history to the present.

examples.zh: 两位老总煮酒论英雄，谈起行业的未来。
examples.en: The two executives talked over wine about heroes and the future of the industry.

story.en: Cao Cao told Liu Bei over a calm talk that the only heroes under heaven were the two of them; the romance later added the scene of plum wine heated in the garden.
story.zh: 曹操从容对刘备说：“今天下英雄，唯使君与操耳。”后世《三国演义》演为青梅煮酒。

usage.en: Cao Cao told Liu Bei that only the two of them were heroes under heaven; the vivid wine-warming scene is from the Romance of the Three Kingdoms (青梅煮酒论英雄).
usage.zh: 曹操对刘备说天下英雄唯使君与操；青梅煮酒的情节见《三国演义》。

literal: set out · general principles · start · rules
natural: lay out general principles and set rules

meaning.en: To set out the main principles and conventions of a book or field.
meaning.zh: 提出全书的大纲和体例，也指首创某种规范。

examples.zh: 这部词典发凡起例，为后世编纂树立了规范。
examples.en: This dictionary laid down the principles and set the standard for later compilers.

examples.zh: 导言部分发凡起例，说明了全书的体例。
examples.en: The introduction sets out the plan and explains how the book is organised.

usage.en: Scholarly; about the opening framework of a work.
usage.zh: 书面语，多指著作的体例、总纲。
